name: Gringo
note: gringo is the Potassco ASP grounder (now inside clingo, potassco.org/clingo); its input language is well documented ('On the Semantics of Gringo', 'On the Input Language of ASP Grounder Gringo'). The LLM's URL potassco.org/gringo/ is 404.

name: Cell BE Assembly
note: The name is descriptive, not a real title. The actual language is the SPU assembly language (IBM's 'SPU Assembly Language Specification' for the Cell BE SPUs).

name: JHDL
note: Java-based HDL from BYU (Bellows & Hutchings, FCCM 1998). There is no Wikipedia page, which is why the LLM's URL is 404, and the old site jhdl.ee.byu.edu is gone.

name: Porth
note: Tsoding's Forth-like concatenative language. The LLM's repository URL github.com/wrp1039/porth is 404.

name: Alpha Assembly
note: The DEC Alpha assembly language ('Alpha Assembly Language Guide', Bryant/CMU; Digital UNIX Assembly Language Programmer's Guide).

name: B-Method
note: The B-Method is a formal method. Its language is B / Abstract Machine Notation (AMN), so 'B-Method' names the method, not the language.

name: UserRPL
note: 'User RPL' is listed as a dialect of HP's RPL, alongside System RPL, on the RPL Wikipedia page.

name: NATJ
note: Nat/J is the Java-to-native (C/Objective-C/C++) binding library of Multi-OS Engine. The LLM's sample is plain Java that imports natj.*, its Wikipedia URL does not exist, and its sample origin github.com/yourusername/natj-example is a placeholder (404).

name: BennuGD
note: Open-source game development suite with its own DIV/Fenix-derived language. The Wikipedia page exists and is in the 'Scripting languages' category.

name: IBM 704 Assembly
note: The 704 assembly language is SAP (Symbolic Assembly Program, later the SHARE Assembly Program), which the IBM 704 page mentions.

name: Oxygen Basic
note: BASIC dialect and compiler (O2) by Charles Pegge. Rosetta Code has Category:OxygenBasic. There is no Wikipedia page.

name: Arena
note: Arena scripting language: C-like syntax and library with automatic memory management (minimalinux.org/arena, FreeBSD port lang/arena, arena(1) man page). There is no Wikipedia page.

name: MLj
note: MLj is a Standard ML '97 to Java bytecode compiler (Benton, Kennedy, Russell, ICFP'98) with Java-interop language extensions. The language is essentially SML plus those extensions.

name: Disciple
note: Disciple is Ben Lippmeier's strict Haskell dialect with effect typing, implemented by the Disciplined Disciple Compiler (DDC) and later evolved into Discus.

name: Agal
note: Adobe Graphics Assembly Language, used for Stage3D shaders. The Wikipedia title redirects to Stage3D, which has an AGAL section.

name: BASIC-D
note: Three searches found no BASIC dialect named 'BASIC-D'. Data General's BASICs are called 'Extended BASIC' and 'Business Basic'. The LLM's evidence URL (Data_General_BASIC) is 404, and its sample is generic Dartmouth-style BASIC from a non-existent origin (github.com/rosettacode-lang/basic, 404). Likely fabricated.

name: KVIrc Script
note: KVIrc's built-in scripting language is called KVS (documented at kvirc.net/doc).

name: kBasic
note: KBasic is a VB6/QBasic-compatible BASIC dialect by Bernd Noetscher. The Wikipedia title redirects to Gambas, which mentions it.

name: Axe
note: Axe (the Axe Parser language) for TI-83+/84+ calculators, by Kevin Horowitz.

name: Electrum
note: Electrum is a temporal extension of the Alloy specification language plus its analyzer (INESC TEC/ONERA, ASE 2018). It is a specification language rather than a programming language.

name: Bedwyr
note: Bedwyr is a logic-programming-based model-checking system (Baelde, Gacek, Miller, Nadathur, Tiu, CADE 2007) with its own lambda-Prolog-like definition language. The LLM's slimmer.gforge.inria.fr URL is dead.

name: Obix
note: OO language by Christian Neumanns that compiles to Java (official site rps-obix.com, github.com/Obix). Wikidata classes it as a programming language. The English Wikipedia article is gone, which is why the URL is 404.

name: Koord
note: DSL for distributed robotics (Ghosh et al., OOPSLA 2020, CyPhyHouse). The LLM's repository name 'Koord-Lang' is wrong; the real repository is KoordLanguage.

name: Argile
note: Compiled, polymorphism-oriented language that generates C (Savannah nongnu). Rosetta Code has Category:Argile. There is no Wikipedia page.

name: VA Smalltalk
note: Instantiations' VA Smalltalk (now the VAST Platform) succeeds IBM VisualAge Smalltalk. It is a Smalltalk implementation/dialect, and the VisualAge page mentions it explicitly.

name: OpenAxiom
note: OpenAxiom is a computer algebra system (a 2007 Axiom fork). Its programming language is SPAD, the Axiom language. The Wikipedia title redirects to Axiom.

name: Brython
note: Real project, but it describes itself as 'a Python 3 implementation for client-side web programming', not a distinct language. Wikipedia 'Brython' is about the Celtic Britons.

name: DSSP
note: Dialog System for Structured Programming: a Forth-like language from Moscow State University (Brusentsov, Setun-70). It is listed on the Wikipedia 'DSSP' disambiguation page, and the libreDSSP interpreter is on GitHub.

name: Pilog
note: Pilog (PicoLisp Prolog) is Prolog embedded in PicoLisp and is documented in the PicoLisp Reference. The LLM's picolisp.com wiki URL is 404.

name: PicBasic
note: microEngineering Labs' PICBASIC / PICBASIC PRO BASIC compilers for PIC microcontrollers (a BASIC dialect). There is no Wikipedia page.

name: ARIBAS
note: Otto Forster's interactive interpreter and language for big-integer and multi-precision arithmetic. There is no Wikipedia page.

name: OVAL
note: MITRE/CIS Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language: a declarative XML-based security-content language, not a general-purpose programming language.

name: Oxymoron
note: No esolangs.org page (the claimed URL is 404, and the esolangs search API and Language list have 0 hits). The only same-named thing is github.com/huiannie/Oxymoron, a compiler for Gaddis textbook pseudocode, which does not match the LLM's claimed esolang or its sample syntax ('output input ... exit execute'). The claimed esolang looks fabricated.

name: Jim Tcl
note: Small-footprint Tcl implementation/dialect (Salvatore Sanfilippo; maintained by Steve Bennett). The LLM's jim.tcl.tk is dead; the current site is jim.tcl-lang.org.

name: Andl
note: 'Andl is A New Database Language' by David M. Bennett: a Third-Manifesto relational language (andl.org, Lambda the Ultimate node 5307). There is no Wikipedia page.

name: DQL
note: Documentum Query Language: the SQL-derived query language of EMC/OpenText Documentum, with official DQL Reference Manuals.

name: Alore
note: Jukka Lehtosalo's Python-like language with optional static typing (a precursor of mypy). alorelang.org is dead.

name: Oblivion Script
note: The scripting language of the TES IV: Oblivion Construction Set (often called ObScript). There is no Wikipedia page, so the URL is 404.

name: WebDSL
note: Domain-specific language for web applications (TU Delft; the compiler is at github.com/webdsl/webdsl). There is no Wikipedia page.

name: Cakelisp
note: Macoy Madson's performance-oriented Lisp-like language that generates C/C++. The GitHub repository (macoy/makuto) is now 404 because it moved to macoy.me.
